claim: Prolonged eye-based attention can bias ocular dominance.
source: Previous research has found that prolonged eye-based attention can bias ocular dominance.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous research in the abstract.

claim: If one eye long-termly views a regular movie meanwhile the opposite eye views a backward movie of the same episode, perceptual ocular dominance will shift towards the eye previously viewing the backward movie.
source: If one eye long-termly views a regular movie meanwhile the opposite eye views a backward movie of the same episode, perceptual ocular dominance will shift towards the eye previously viewing the backward movie.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous research in the abstract.

claim: The frontal eye field (FEF) and intraparietal sulcus (IPS) show robust activation when participants watch dichoptic movies while focusing attention on the regular movie.
source: We found robust activation of the frontal eye field (FEF) and intraparietal sulcus (IPS) when participants were watching the dichoptic movie while focusing their attention on the regular movie.
evidence: This is a direct finding from the fMRI experiment reported in the manuscript.

claim: A robust effect of attention-induced ocular dominance shift occurs when the cortical function of vertex or IPS is transiently inhibited by continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS).
source: Interestingly, we found a robust effect of attention-induced ocular dominance shift when the cortical function of vertex or IPS was transiently inhibited by continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS), yet the effect was significantly attenuated to a negligible extent when cTBS was delivered to FEF.
evidence: This is a direct finding from Experiment 2 using TMS.

claim: The effect of attention-induced ocular dominance shift is significantly attenuated to a negligible extent when cTBS is delivered to FEF.
source: Interestingly, we found a robust effect of attention-induced ocular dominance shift when the cortical function of vertex or IPS was transiently inhibited by continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS), yet the effect was significantly attenuated to a negligible extent when cTBS was delivered to FEF.
evidence: This is a direct finding from Experiment 2 using TMS.

claim: The attenuation of ocular dominance shift after inhibitory stimulation of FEF is not due to any impact of the cTBS on the binocular rivalry measurement of ocular dominance.
source: A control experiment verified that the attenuation of ocular dominance shift after inhibitory stimulation of FEF was not due to any impact of the cTBS on the binocular rivalry measurement of ocular dominance.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from a control experiment (Experiment 3).

claim: The fronto-parietal attentional network is involved in controlling eye-based attention in the 'dichoptic-backward-movie' adaptation paradigm.
source: These findings suggest that the fronto-parietal attentional network is involved in controlling eye-based attention in the 'dichoptic-backward-movie' adaptation paradigm, and in this network, FEF plays a crucial causal role in generating the attention-induced ocular dominance shift.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: FEF plays a crucial causal role in generating the attention-induced ocular dominance shift.
source: These findings suggest that the fronto-parietal attentional network is involved in controlling eye-based attention in the 'dichoptic-backward-movie' adaptation paradigm, and in this network, FEF plays a crucial causal role in generating the attention-induced ocular dominance shift.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Selective attention allows for the selection of pertinent information from a vast array of input for further cognitive processing.
source: Selective attention allows for the selection of pertinent information from a vast array of input for further cognitive processing (Treisman, 1969; Wolfe et al., 1989).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: Attentional selection can be location-specific.
source: It has been well known that attentional selection can be location-specific (Posner, 1980), feature-specific (Corbetta et al., 1990), or object-specific (Egly et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Attentional selection can be feature-specific.
source: It has been well known that attentional selection can be location-specific (Posner, 1980), feature-specific (Corbetta et al., 1990), or object-specific (Egly et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Attentional selection can be object-specific.
source: It has been well known that attentional selection can be location-specific (Posner, 1980), feature-specific (Corbetta et al., 1990), or object-specific (Egly et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Selective attention can be based on the eye of origin for visual input, named eye-based attention.
source: Notably, selective attention can also be based on the eye of origin for visual input, named eye-based attention (Neisser and Becklen, 1975).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Presenting top-down attentional cues to one eye can intensify the competition strength of input signals in the attended eye during binocular rivalry.
source: For instance, presenting top-down attentional cues to one eye can intensify the competition strength of input signals in the attended eye during binocular rivalry (Choe and Kim, 2022; Zhang et al., 2012) and shift the eye balance towards the attended eye (Wong et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous research with citations.

claim: Presenting top-down attentional cues to one eye can shift the eye balance towards the attended eye.
source: For instance, presenting top-down attentional cues to one eye can intensify the competition strength of input signals in the attended eye during binocular rivalry (Choe and Kim, 2022; Zhang et al., 2012) and shift the eye balance towards the attended eye (Wong et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous research with citation.

claim: Eye-based attention exerts real-time effects on information processing.
source: It is worth noting that eye-based attention not only exerts real-time effects on information processing (Choe and Kim, 2022; Wong et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2012), but also exhibits a counterintuitive perceptual aftereffect that prolonged attention to a monocular pathway (or eye-based attention) can result in a shift of ocular dominance towards the unattended eye (Song et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous research with citations.

claim: Prolonged attention to a monocular pathway can result in a shift of ocular dominance towards the unattended eye.
source: It is worth noting that eye-based attention not only exerts real-time effects on information processing (Choe and Kim, 2022; Wong et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2012), but also exhibits a counterintuitive perceptual aftereffect that prolonged attention to a monocular pathway (or eye-based attention) can result in a shift of ocular dominance towards the unattended eye (Song et al., 2023; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous research with citations.

claim: The predominance of the unattended eye in binocular rivalry increased after 1 hr of adaptation to the 'dichoptic-backward-movie'.
source: Song et al., 2023 found that the predominance of the unattended eye in binocular rivalry increased after 1 hr of adaptation to the 'dichoptic-backward-movie,' indicating a shift of perceptual ocular dominance towards the unattended eye.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous research (Song et al., 2023).

claim: The change of ocular dominance after adaptation is thought to result from unbalanced eye-based attention rather than unbalanced input energy.
source: Since the overall energy of visual input from the two eyes was balanced throughout the adaptation period, the change of ocular dominance after adaptation is thought to result from unbalanced eye-based attention rather than unbalanced input energy as in typical short-term monocular deprivation (Bai et al., 2017; Lunghi et al., 2011; Zhou et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings based on the experimental design.

claim: Steady-state visually evoked potentials (SSVEPs) elicited by the adapting stimuli in each eye were observed in both the occipital and frontal sites.
source: Furthermore, the steady-state visually evoked potentials (SSVEPs) elicited by the adapting stimuli in each eye were observed in both the occipital and frontal sites (Song et al., 2023), with a significant positive correlation between the frontal neural-activity index (a normalized SSVEP response related to selective attention) and the shift of perceptual ocular dominance.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous research (Song et al., 2023).

claim: There is a significant positive correlation between the frontal neural-activity index and the shift of perceptual ocular dominance.
source: Furthermore, the steady-state visually evoked potentials (SSVEPs) elicited by the adapting stimuli in each eye were observed in both the occipital and frontal sites (Song et al., 2023), with a significant positive correlation between the frontal neural-activity index (a normalized SSVEP response related to selective attention) and the shift of perceptual ocular dominance.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous research (Song et al., 2023).

claim: The frontal activation observed by Song et al., 2023 is primarily located in the frontal pole.
source: Besides, the frontal activation observed by Song et al., 2023 is primarily located in the frontal pole, which is not considered a key area directly responsible for attentional control (Iidaka, 2017; Jääskeläinen et al., 2016; Leminen et al., 2020; Xie et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from previous research with citations.

claim: The frontal pole is not considered a key area directly responsible for attentional control.
source: Besides, the frontal activation observed by Song et al., 2023 is primarily located in the frontal pole, which is not considered a key area directly responsible for attentional control (Iidaka, 2017; Jääskeläinen et al., 2016; Leminen et al., 2020; Xie et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations.

claim: SSVEP is limited to detecting brain activities that oscillate at the flickering frequency (and its harmonics) of the visual stimulus.
source: As SSVEP is limited to detecting brain activities that oscillate at the flickering frequency (and its harmonics) of the visual stimulus, brain activities that do not precisely align with the flickering frequency may be missed (Norcia et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the SSVEP method with citation.

claim: Brain activities that do not precisely align with the flickering frequency may be missed by SSVEP.
source: As SSVEP is limited to detecting brain activities that oscillate at the flickering frequency (and its harmonics) of the visual stimulus, brain activities that do not precisely align with the flickering frequency may be missed (Norcia et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the SSVEP method with citation.

claim: The parietal and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex are typical brain regions associated with the attentional network.
source: Consequently, the activities of typical brain regions associated with the attentional network, such as the parietal and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (Vossel et al., 2014), may not be captured by the SSVEP measures.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: Participants exhibited high response accuracy (M=91.67%, SD = 14.91%) to questions about the movie plot after each experimental run.
source: The results showed a high response accuracy to the questions (M=91.67%, SD = 14.91%), indicating that the participants had paid close attention to the regular movie and clearly understood the plot.
evidence: This is a direct finding from Experiment 1.

claim: Participants exhibited reasonable performance in the RSVP task (d'=3.33, SD=0.83) in the control runs.
source: In the control runs, participants also exhibited a reasonable performance in the RSVP task (d'=3.33, SD=0.83).
evidence: This is a direct finding from Experiment 1.

claim: There was no significant main effect or interaction of experiment condition and run on d-prime score in the RSVP task (ps >0.09).
source: A 2 (experiment condition: dichoptic, binocular)×3 (run: run1, run2, run3) repeated measurements analysis of variance (ANOVA) was conducted on the d-prime score, which indicated no significant main effect or interaction (ps >0.09).
evidence: This is a direct finding from statistical analysis in Experiment 1.

claim: Four clusters showed stronger responses to the dichoptic movies than to the binocular movies in the experimental runs.
source: We found four clusters showing stronger responses to the dichoptic movies than to the binocular movies, especially in the experimental runs (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a direct finding from fMRI analysis in Experiment 1, with reference to Figure 3.

claim: The four clusters showing stronger responses to dichoptic movies are located in the right FEF, bilateral IPS, and the right superior parietal lobule (SPL).
source: They are located in the right FEF, bilateral IPS, and the right superior parietal lobule (SPL).
evidence: This is a direct finding from fMRI analysis in Experiment 1.

claim: In the control runs, the responses of the identified brain areas to the dichoptic and binocular movies showed no discernible difference.
source: In the control runs, the responses of these areas to the dichoptic and binocular movies showed no discernible difference.
evidence: This is a direct finding from fMRI analysis in Experiment 1.

claim: The right FEF, bilateral IPS, and right SPL are part of the dorsal attentional network.
source: As previous research has demonstrated that these brain areas are part of the dorsal attentional network (Vossel et al., 2014), we therefore speculate that the identified clusters would be responsible for eye-based attention.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation.

claim: The identified clusters (right FEF, bilateral IPS, right SPL) are responsible for eye-based attention.
source: As previous research has demonstrated that these brain areas are part of the dorsal attentional network (Vossel et al., 2014), we therefore speculate that the identified clusters would be responsible for eye-based attention.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the fMRI findings and previous research.
